key_risks: Rapid de-escalation or negotiated Hormuz resolution could crater crude prices and reverse energy gains
A soft June/July CPI print could rally growth/tech and QQQ, causing this value/energy tilt to lag SPY
Demand destruction from an oil shock could hit energy equities alongside broad markets
USO futures roll and volatility can erode returns even if spot crude stays elevated

portfolio.rationale: Direct beneficiary of Hormuz blockade escalation and Brent at $83; equities lag spot crude and offer upside with less curve decay than USO.
Highest-torque exposure to supply disruption from the July 14 blockade; negative beta to SPY hedges equity drawdown.
Value with energy/financials tilt outperforms growth when 10y yields rise to 4.61% and inflation runs 4.2%.
Defensive equity holding up well (+2.8% 30d vs SPY) amid geopolitical stress and rate pressure; near-zero beta cushions selloff.
Cash-like yield with no duration risk while yields rise and rate-cut odds fade on hot CPI.

portfolio_rationale: An escalating Hormuz blockade, oil supply shock, sticky 4.2% CPI, and rising yields favor energy and value over rate-sensitive growth/tech, which was already selling off into the entry. Defensive low-vol and T-bills buffer against a broad risk-off move over the month.
rationale_summary: Overweight energy and value for the oil supply shock and inflation backdrop, with low-vol and T-bill ballast against geopolitically driven equity weakness; underweight rate-sensitive growth.
